name: All files access
plain: Gives the app access to nearly all files on the device.
meaning: Lets an app read and write most user files. Intended for file managers and backup tools; Play requires a declaration.

android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > All files access
android.store_policy: Play: declaration form; only for core file management, backup, antivirus
android.note: Does not reach Android/data on Android 11+.

ios.note: No all-files access exists; apps use the document picker.

limits.headline: Can open almost every file on your Android phone if you turn on All files access
limits.user_action: You open Settings and switch on All files access for the app
can: List and open files across your Android shared storage
Change, move and delete files in those shared folders
Run file manager, backup and cleaner features
Keep the access until you switch it off in Settings
cannot: Reach other apps' private folders in Android/data on Android 11 and newer
Be turned on from a pop up; you must use Settings
Exist on iPhone; apps use the document picker instead
Be approved easily on Google Play; the store limits it to apps that truly need it
limits.differs: Android only. iPhone has no all files access; apps only get files you pick.

story.what_it_is: Gives an app wide access to nearly all files on the phone.

marketing.name: All files access
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: a special access for apps like file managers and backup tools that need to manage most files.

story.for_you: You are sent to a special Settings page to turn this on, not a normal pop up. Once on, the app can see and change most files. Only file managers and backup apps should need it.
story.for_makers: Needed by file managers, antivirus and backup tools. Google Play makes developers fill out a declaration and says no for most apps that only need photos or documents.

use_cases.example: A file manager lets you browse every folder on your phone and move files around.
An antivirus app scans every file on the phone for malware.
A backup app copies all your documents and photos to the cloud.
A game mod manager reads and writes other games' folders to install mods.
A coding app on the phone opens project folders anywhere on storage.
A music player scans every folder for audio files.

risks: Can read most of your files
story.android_note: Special app access granted in Settings, and Play requires a declaration.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no such access, since apps can only see their own sandbox.
